chantedPrayers.text: Liberating Prayer O Blessed One, Shakyamuni Buddha, precious Treasury of Compassion, Bestower of Supreme Inner Peace. You who love all beings without exception are the source of happiness and goodness, and you guide us to the liberating path. Your body is a wish-fulfilling jewel, your speech is supreme, purifying nectar, and your mind is refuge for all living beings. With folded palms I turn to you, Supreme unchanging Friend. I request from the depths of my heart, please give me the light of your wisdom to dispel the darkness of my mind and to heal my mental continuum. Please nourish me with your goodness, that I in turn may nourish all beings with an unceasing banquet of delight. Through your compassionate intention, your blessings and virtuous deeds, and my strong wish to rely upon you, may all suffering quickly cease and all happiness and joy be fulfilled, and may holy Dharma flourish forevermore.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Five Mahayana Paths introduction and Ten Mahayana Grounds
teaching.text:
Okay, so as I mentioned, we'll look a little bit at the Five Mahayana Paths. Which, perhaps you know, at the temple we have five paths, and they're named after these five. Which is lovely, because then when random visitors come, they're like, where's the path of seeing? I walked the path of accumulation. And it's fantastic. And there's Clear Light Road, that's the last one. And so they create a little karma every time they say that.

Okay, so this is from Joyful Path of Good Fortune. If we want to know more about the grounds and paths, these five are explained — yeah, this is the most extensive explanation of the five themselves. But then from path three to five, basically from the path of seeing to the path of no more learning, that's explained — that's what Ocean of Nectar is. Ocean of Nectar is just that. There's nothing other than that that Ocean of Nectar is. It's just explaining from the path of seeing, which is when you begin, when you start to enter what's called the Ten Mahayana Grounds. So from basically three to five, there's ten.

So you kind of finish the path of seeing, and then you enter what's called Very Joyful, and then you progress along the Ten Mahayana Grounds. And so that's what this book is. It just explains the Ten Mahayana Grounds. So if you want to know about the details of all the different grounds, and especially what's going on between three and five, then you can read Ocean of Nectar.

Okay, so let me just read the ground names, just to have the transmission of that, and then we can talk about the five. How are we doing so far? So there's Five Mahayana Paths: Path of Accumulation, Path of Preparation, Path of Seeing, Path of Meditation, Path of No More Learning.

Then basically as you journey from the Path of Seeing, which is when you directly realize emptiness with a mind of bodhichitta — you're officially on the Path of Seeing when you do that. You directly realize emptiness with a mind of spontaneous bodhichitta, Path of Seeing. Basically when you do that, then as you start to meditate on emptiness more and more, you're now sort of on the Path of Meditation, and basically as you traverse through the Path of Meditation, the fourth of the five, and then you go through the fifth, Path of No More Learning, that's divided into ten parts.

Okay, one, two, three, four, five, and then from three to five, there's a tenfold little division in there. Okay, and that's the Ten Mahayana Grounds. David, do you have a hand there somewhere?

teaching.speaker: David
teaching.text: So do each of the ten correspond to one of the three, four, five, or is that not an appropriate question?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Ten Ground names, VSLR DAGEGSI mnemonic, nine levels of innate self-grasping, full path overview through enlightenment
teaching.text:
No, they mostly happen on four. They're mostly broken up in that, and then it gets a bit hazy towards the fifth. Yeah.

I'll just read the ten, just so we have the words. They're amazing words to have. So: Very Joyful, Stainless, Luminous, Radiant, Difficult to Overcome, Approaching, Gone Afar, Immovable, Good Intelligence, Cloud of Dharma.

VSLR DAGEGSI. Obviously. DAGEGSI. There you go. VSLR DAGEGSI. That's how you remember it. Very Joyful — that's V. S — Stainless. L — Luminous. R — Radiant. VSLR DAGEGSI. Difficult to Overcome, Approaching, Gone Afar. DAGEG. Immovable, Good Intelligence, and Cloud of Dharma. Yeah, DAGEGSI. Good Intelligence is the ninth ground. Cloud of Dharma.

Cloud of Dharma, page 34, Ocean of Nectar. Basically what's going on there is, once we realize emptiness directly, that basically means that we're realizing emptiness without a generic image. That's all that means. So there's no mental construction of emptiness. We're seeing it directly like you'd see a chair or something.

But why aren't you a Buddha yet? It's basically because there are all these obstructions to enlightenment in the mind. And then you start to work through all of them as you go through. And they're called big-big, middling-big, small-big, et cetera. All the way to small-small. So there's nine of them.

Okay, anyway. We can't just keep going on random digressions. I just wanted to at least read those.

So the Five Mahayana Paths. So the point of this is to rejoice in it and to start to imagine them. That's the kind of idea of this.

Okay, Five Mahayana Paths. Path of Accumulation. Path of Preparation. Path of Seeing. Path of Meditation. Path of No More Learning. APSMAL. Easy. APSMAL. We've got to know these, though. You've got to have these. Like naming the boroughs. It should just be like: Accumulation, Preparation, Path of Seeing, Meditation, No More Learning. APSMAL.

Anyway. They're called paths because just as external paths lead us to our destination, so these internal paths lead us to our ultimate destination: full enlightenment. They can also be called grounds because just as the ground acts as the basis for the growth of plants, trees, and crops, so spiritual grounds are the basis for all spiritual qualities.

We enter the Mahayana Path of Accumulation when we generate spontaneous bodhichitta and become a Bodhisattva. Okay, that's the marker. So you basically have spontaneous bodhichitta, which somewhat you could just say means you've got tranquil abiding on bodhichitta. Good enough explanation, yeah.

Basically you don't have to think about generating bodhichitta anymore. It's suffused with the mind. Every moment of the mind, while you're sleeping, while you're walking around, you don't have to put any effort into generating it ever again. It's like how self-grasping is spontaneous right now. We don't put any effort into generating self-grasping. So it's like that, but with bodhichitta. Just thinking about that and imagining what that would be like is amazing. Wow, every moment of every day, bodhichitta is there without any effort.

So let's go to the Path of Accumulation. All the virtuous minds of a Bodhisattva at this stage, such as the minds of love, compassion, bodhichitta, and the wisdom realizing emptiness are Mahayana Paths of Accumulation. By virtue of the spontaneous attainment of bodhichitta, the realizations of method and wisdom within the mind of a Bodhisattva are greatly superior to the realizations of Hinayanists.

It's then divided into three. I don't think we're going to do that. Anyway, yeah, for the sake of time. But you can read it in Joyful Path. It's just five or six pages.

The Mahayana Path of Preparation is so called because the Bodhisattva is now preparing for a direct realization of emptiness. At this point, the Bodhisattva's meditation on emptiness is still conceptual. That is, emptiness still appears to his or her mind mixed with a mental image.

Conceptual just means that we're perceiving something with a mental image instead of just perceiving the thing directly. You can perceive something directly without needing a mental image. This is how our senses are perceiving things usually, like seeing this microphone. The black color of the microphone that we're seeing with our eyes is direct. It's not mediated through a mental image. The eye part, when you think about it, it is. But the eyes, they're just seeing it directly.

Conceptual mind is just the mental image you have about something. The reason we want to get rid of those is because we want to see the thing directly. The aim of Buddhism isn't just no conceptions in general. It's no — we want to see emptiness directly, without a medium. Until we get rid of our conceptual understanding of emptiness, we can't see it directly.

In the scriptures, the analogy is like an ice. It's like a window made of ice, something like this. It's translucent at first, and then as you meditate more and more and more on emptiness, it starts to melt. That's the conceptual idea of emptiness. Eventually it melts completely, and you see it directly, instead of through a veil or through an ice wall of some sort.

The point is, at the Path of Preparation, we still have a conceptual idea of emptiness. We have a mental image of it. We're still quite an amazing being at this point. We're a Bodhisattva, but we still have this mental concept of emptiness that we're holding on to.

The goal of the Mahayana Path of Preparation is to bring the mind and its object, emptiness, closer and closer until they eventually mix completely. The mental image dissolves, and all dualistic appearance subsides into emptiness. This is accomplished through repeated meditation on emptiness with a union of tranquil abiding and superior seeing.

So the point that we say someone's moved from the Path of Accumulation to the Path of Preparation — the sort of marker, the gate that you kind of go through — is that the Path of Accumulation was spontaneous bodhichitta. Now I enter the Path of Preparation when I have tranquil abiding on emptiness. It's not a direct realization of emptiness yet, because it's still conceptual. It's still a concept that we're holding. But we have tranquil abiding on it, which means it's an immovable concentration.

It would look like enlightenment for most people at first. You'd think, I must be enlightened. Every moment of every day, I'm perceiving emptiness with a spontaneous bodhichitta. And then the bliss that's suffusing your mind at this point is unbelievable. It's like too much to handle. Not really, because there's no self really left. But anyway, it's an incredible realization, just this.

As you go through the Path of Preparation, there's four stages. We're not going to get into all of them, but I'll just tell you the names for fun: Heat, Peak, Patience, and Supreme Dharma. Very cool. Good to know about.

Then we continue to meditate on emptiness with our tranquil abiding and superior seeing. More, more, more, more, more. And basically our dualistic appearances reduce and reduce and reduce and reduce and reduce. And then finally they reduce altogether, and then we see emptiness directly for the first time. Which simply means sans generic image. Sans a concept of it. Without a concept of it.

Okay. Then you're on the Path of Seeing. You can meditate on emptiness directly. And basically at this point, you abandon all intellectually-formed self-grasping, all intellectually-formed delusions. So all the sort of weird ideas that you've surmised about the world that are wrong, just through bad reasoning.

Like we have tons of these, but we're not aware of them. It's like Geshe-la was saying, the way ordinary people talk sounds crazy to a realized being. Because there's so many layers of confusion that they're talking about as if they're facts. You just sound like you should be locked up, basically. From the point of view of someone with realizations, it's just all complete nonsense.

So it's hard for them not to laugh at us. But they have so much compassion, they don't laugh. But they don't take ordinary beings very seriously. You're not offended by them. It's just completely crazy. It's like, okay, yeah, sure, okay. Love you. Like that. Very respectful, but there's not this issue with them. You just seem crazy.

So anyway, you abandon all these weird ideas about life and the world that you come up with just through bad reasoning. There's still what's called the innate delusions, which are the ones that have been with us for countless eons. Attachment, hatred, ignorance.

So basically while you're on the Path of Seeing, you start to meditate on emptiness with the direct realization. And then while you're doing that, you sort of progress onto what's called the first Mahayana Ground. So you're still on the Path of Seeing. And then while you're on the first Mahayana Ground, Very Joyful, you then progress into the Path of Meditation. It sort of bridges the two. I'm not going to get into all the specific details of that. But it's all in Ocean of Nectar, if you'd like.

So then Geshe-la says, you still need to abandon innate self-grasping. This is specifically what we're getting rid of. Not the other general delusions. It's innate self-grasping specifically. So there are nine levels of innate self-grasping: big-big, middling-big, small-big, big-middling, middling-middling, small-middling. We can each get a name in class, okay? Who wants to be big-big? Okay, that's Alexis. Middling-big? Okay, no, we won't make it. Ryan, which one do you want to be? Middling-middling. Yeah, I can see how excited you are over there. Okay, so you're middling-middling.

Bodhisattvas on the Path of Seeing enter meditative equipoise on emptiness to overcome big-big innate self-grasping. When their wisdom of meditative equipoise becomes powerful enough to act as the direct antidote to big-big innate self-grasping, it's transformed into the wisdom of meditative equipoise on the uninterrupted path, the meditation of the first ground. So now you're officially on the first ground, Very Joyful. You abandon big-big innate self-grasping. When this abandonment has occurred, you then move to the second ground, Stainless, and so on.

Okay, so then you progress through the Path of Meditation. That's going through the different Mahayana Grounds. You're getting rid of all the different problems and obstacles in the mind. You're eroding them away.

And then on the eighth ground, Bodhisattvas have abandoned all self-grasping and all delusions. But they still have obstructions to omniscience. So they have no delusions at all. Zero. Including not even a little self-grasping. But they still have what's called the obstructions to omniscience. That's the garlic smell. I think we mentioned that last week.

They once again enter meditation on emptiness, and when they've abandoned the gross obstructions to omniscience, they advance to the ninth ground. Bodhisattvas on the ninth ground again enter meditative equipoise and abandon the subtle obstructions to omniscience, thus advancing to the tenth ground.

And when Bodhisattvas on the tenth ground enter meditative equipoise on emptiness, their wisdom becomes powerful enough to act as a direct antidote to the very subtle obstructions to omniscience. This concentration is known as the Vajra-like concentration of the Path of Meditation. It's also called the exalted wisdom of the final continuum, because it is the last moment of the mind of a sentient being.

What an amazing moment, right? We only have one of these ever. But you can imagine what that would be like. And at this point, you can see all your past and future lives. You can see it all clearly. And you're like, I'm finally done. I'm no longer a sentient being after this moment.

In the next moment, the Bodhisattva becomes a Buddha. In one session, Bodhisattvas free themselves from the various subtle obstructions to omniscience and attain the final released path, the Mahayana Path of No More Learning. When this path is attained, the Bodhisattva has become a Buddha and has gained the exalted omniscient wisdom. This time, the meditator attains the four bodies of a Buddha.

Bodhisattvas on the tenth ground have many emanations, and they become Buddhas. All their emanations become Buddhas and work for the benefit of all living beings. Which is very cool to think about. You have a bunch of emanations up to that point. And even when you're on Very Joyful, you start to be able to emanate beings to help people. And emanate stuff to help people. And then it basically increases — the amount of emanations you get increase exponentially as you go. Something like that.

So you have a hundred, and then you have a thousand, and then you have ten thousand or a hundred thousand, whatever it is. And it just keeps going. So at this point you have whatever, a hundred trillion bajillion emanations, and they all become Buddhas. Helping people.

Okay. Anyone have questions about that? Yeah, Jose, please.

teaching.speaker: Jose
teaching.text: Not really about that, but related. There's also the book on Tantric Grounds and Paths. So what part does that one cover?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Tantric grounds and paths vs. Sutra grounds and paths
teaching.text:
Oh, you're really throwing a wrench in this one. Yeah, so there's also the Tantric Grounds and Paths. And the Tantric Grounds and Paths are different than these five. I know, I'm sorry. Awful to even know about.

Yeah, there's Hinayana ones too. We don't really need to know those. But yeah, there's the Tantric Grounds and Paths. And so what marks each stage is a bit different. So for example, the Path of Seeing, according to Highest Yoga Tantra, is when you attain what's called meaning clear light. Which is, you realize emptiness directly, but with your clear light mind. Yeah, so when you do that, you get to the third ground. And then when you — I'm not going to go through this right now.

So learning these originally, if you don't have a tantric practice, this is your path. This is the only path you can follow to enlightenment. So you learn them, you practice it, you progress along them. But if you get the initiations of Highest Yoga Tantra, then you can progress along the Tantric Grounds and Paths.

It's still useful to know, because we still need to do all these things. We need to generate bodhichitta, realize emptiness with our bodhichitta mind, realize it directly, and then go deeper, deeper, deeper into it. So yeah, all that is still kind of relevant. But yeah, we do at some point kind of transpose over to the Tantric Grounds and Paths.

David, do you have anything? Oh, no, you didn't. Anne, Alexis, Ryan.

teaching.speaker: Anne K
teaching.text: Remind me, tell us again when we start emanating. Very interested in that. And then the second thing is, do you have any ideas for how to imagine what this is like beyond just letting the words drift around in our mind?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Reading the Twelve Special Qualities from Ocean of Nectar (p. 403)
teaching.text:
Yeah. How to kind of bring it alive. First thing about emanations, let me read this very special section of Ocean of Nectar, where Geshe-la tries to describe — I would say this is the kind of thing very hard to put in words, but thankfully all these great Buddhist teachers of the past did, to the best of their ability.

So let me read what's called the Twelve Special Qualities. This has to do with the emanations that you mentioned. But it's nice because each quality has a kind of vividness to it. And then it will help us imagine these grounds better, which is how you bring it alive, which is your second question.

Okay, let me just read the twelve, but the verses are extremely beautiful if you want to read them sometime. This is page 403 of Ocean of Nectar. It's the second page of the Good Qualities of the Ten Grounds. I think this is a slightly older version, so it might not be 403 in your version, but it's the second page of the Good Qualities of the Ten Grounds, which is towards the back.

So, okay, I've attained Very Joyful. I'm basically like, I've realized emptiness directly. I've finally realized emptiness directly with the bodhichitta mind. What then? What's going on with me? Why am I useful?

So at that point, you can see a hundred Buddhas in one short instant. So anytime you want. Just perceive them and have a chat. Realize their blessings in one short instant. Remain alive for a hundred eons. So eons, like a million years or something like that. I forget what the exact number is, but it's a long time. See the ends of the previous hundred eons and the next hundred eons in one short instant.

So you're playing a very long game all of a sudden. You're playing this kind of chess thing over thousands of lives, and you're thinking when you talk to someone, okay, how much can I help in this life and then the next life and then two hundred lives from now? Okay, let me say the right thing and do the right thing. Okay, I'll do this. They might hate me in this life, but it's going to lead them to enlightenment in three hundred lives, and that's the best way to get them there. So that's what I'll do. It's this sort of thing. Your mind is sort of incredible, right?

Enter into and rise from the absorptions of a hundred concentrations in one short instant. Cause a hundred worlds to shake through your magical powers in one short instant. No idea what that means. But I think it has to do with the fact that at this point you so closely see that everything is like a dream. So closely that you can manipulate things with your mind, just like you can in a dream. You're sort of so intimately aware that everything is like a dream, that the boundaries of everything, the different worlds, they just seem like appearances to mind. So you can just sort of visit wherever you want to go and do whatever you want to do. Just like in a dream. Just like in this sort of lucid dream that you're becoming lucid in.

So you have a lot of power all of a sudden. Illuminate a hundred worldly realms through your magical powers in one instant, so you can shake them and illuminate them. Cause a hundred living beings to ripen through magical emanations in one short instant. Visit a hundred Buddha lands in one short instant. Completely open a hundred doors of Dharma in one short instant. Cause a hundred different bodies to be displayed through your body in one short instant. Endow each of these hundred bodies with a retinue of a hundred conqueror sons.

So basically what happens then as you go from two to ten, it just keeps exponentially growing. So the verse here, or Geshe-la's explanation: whereas the Bodhisattva abiding on Very Joyful attains these twelve qualities in hundreds, the Bodhisattva abiding on the second ground, Stainless, attains them in thousands. This means that in one short instant they can see a thousand Buddhas and so forth. On the third ground, the Bodhisattva attains a hundred thousand of these twelve qualities. On the fourth, a thousand million.

teaching.speaker: Grady
teaching.note: Reading continuation of the exponential growth of qualities
teaching.text: On the fifth, ten thousand million. On the sixth ground, a billion. On the seventh ground, a hundred thousand trillion. On the seventh ground, you're just cruising.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Atisha story, 'useless Buddha,' karmic connections, self-generation practice at each path level
teaching.text:
Obviously, people need karma to be able to be helped by you. You're not like a creator god where people are independent of their karma. You're not omnipotent. There's no omnipotence in Buddhism. But basically the karma people have to be helped by you, you now become incredibly useful with that karma.

This is like Geshe-la's example from — I think I've given this in TTP before — but he was talking about Atisha's life story where he's told by Tara: if you rely on action mudra right now, like a consort, you can become enlightened right now. But it would be much more beneficial if you became ordained and became a teacher. And that actually will help a lot more people if you become a teacher right now.

Which is a sort of cryptic puzzle in Atisha's life story. It's always included at this point. So you should think, wait, why would you not become a Buddha? Look at all these things you could do. Why would you be a teacher?

And so in Geshe-la's commentary to it, he's just trying to help people understand. He brought it up in a teaching on advice for teachers. And he said, I've thought a lot about this. I always wondered about this ever since I was a kid. This is part of Atisha's biography at this point. It's included in the canonical story. Why? Why? Why?

And then he said through talking to his teachers and thinking about it, basically the point was that Atisha needed to have these karmic connections with people or else he'd be like a useless Buddha. That was Geshe-la's phrase. Useless Buddha. Basically you have all these spiritual qualities but you have no links to people. So you're just sort of floating around with all this power but you're not linked to anyone.

It's not a definitive thing I'm trying to make here. The point is about making connections and karmic links to people. It's a really nice practical takeaway. As we gain these abilities, we're able to help in this huge way. We have to be connected to people. We have to have links to people. It's just nice to think in our daily life, as we grow, we're going to get wiser and wiser. But we want to be connected to people. We want to have links. We want to reach out to people. So that we can help more and more people as we grow as a person.

Anyway, so that's just some of the fun stuff that's in Ocean of Nectar about this. There's other fun stuff throughout this chapter and the Resulting Grounds chapter about all the good qualities of Bodhisattvas and Buddhas. So that's one way to bring it alive for ourselves — to start to think about those qualities and imagine what it would be like to have them. So that's one way to think about it.

The second way is similar but a little bit different, which is to do a self-generation practice, but where we generate as someone on the different Mahayana paths. So for example, we self-generate as the Bodhisattva on the Path of Accumulation. Which is the first moment we actually become a Bodhisattva. And just imagining and envisioning — what's it like to have spontaneous bodhichitta? Okay, it means I have tranquil abiding. So every moment, every day, I'm focused on bodhichitta. So I have tranquil abiding on bodhichitta. What would that be like?

And so we can try to start to imagine that. Envision that. What is it like to have tranquil abiding? To have that kind of focus, that immovable mind. For example, we start to gain the clairvoyances. Eye clairvoyance, et cetera. Ability to know others' minds. So, okay, what's that like? To have the clairvoyances. To be able to know everyone's mind. A lot of people's minds. So we can imagine that.

Then we can imagine the Path of Preparation. So having tranquil abiding on emptiness. We can visit some of the descriptions of this, like: all attractive and unattractive appearances basically seem completely equal in emptiness. Everything just feels like the magical play of the mind. And there's no higher, lower, here, there, self, other, samsara. Everything is equal in the peace of emptiness. What would it be like to have that experience?

And then Path of Seeing, Meditation, and then No More Learning. And then we can even go through the ten grounds and imagine those different ones. Like on Luminous, everything appears with a golden hue. Very exciting. For some weird karmic reason, everything has this sort of golden hue to it, glow to it. That's why it's called Luminous.

Anyway, we can think about that. We can think about Stainless, which is the name for the second ground where we gain a surpassing perfection of moral discipline. The first six grounds follow the six perfections. So the first is, you basically have perfected giving. The second one, you perfected moral discipline. The third, you perfected patience. Fourth, effort. Fifth, concentration. Sixth, wisdom.

So we can think about — what would it be like to have a surpassing perfection of moral discipline? It's called Stainless. Wow, so beautiful, right? And part of the reason it's stainless is because it's practiced while always remembering emptiness. Similar to the rejoicing point, that it makes it pure when we remember emptiness. So too, when we practice moral discipline, it only becomes pure when we remember emptiness.

So those are a couple of ideas. I don't think we got to Ryan's point. Okay, come on. Come on, come on. Mimi, if it's quick, we can do you too, and then we'll discuss.

teaching.speaker: Ryan
teaching.text: Yeah, quick. I have bad news and good news. The bad news is I'm not even nothing close to understanding anything of the paths. That's fine, that's not bad news. And I accept it's my karma. Maybe one day, maybe not. The good news is I do feel I'm on a better path to opening my heart to love people. So I'm good on that path. So I see some — so at least I feel I got some Amtrak ticket, like an analogy. So even if I don't see all that path, I'm good at least. That's some good news.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text: Yeah, definitely. And just hearing about it is the first step. Then the karmic seeds start getting planted and then eventually the wisdom will come. But we do need the blessing and lineage of just hearing about it. And then understanding and insight will come. Mimi, yeah?

teaching.speaker: Mimi
teaching.text: So it's not so much a question, it's just what came into my mind when you were reading about the emanations. And I just thought, well, if all these beings have emanations and they have links, then there's an emanation that's linked to me. And that anybody can be an emanation. And that's all.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Emanations everywhere, London for the Queen, the man outside the window
teaching.text:
Exactly, yeah. And that's a very important thing to ponder. And over time we'll develop a kind of incontrovertible sort of logical feeling that that's the case, based on what you just described. It's like, countless holy beings that are emanating. I'm definitely in connection with at least one of them. Or else I wouldn't have appeared on this path. There has to be a connection. And I've learned about lots of other Buddhas, so I obviously have connections to all of them. And since they have countless emanations, then there's a ton kicking around in my life. It might just appear in things like our house and our dog and stuff, or our job. But there also could be more things than that, yeah.

And when we start to look for it, they appear everywhere. It's like the point that Geshe-la made once, where he said that London was just emanated for the Queen. What in the world does that mean? Anyway, but he said that. And he said the point was that emanations don't have a history. They don't have an inherent history, but nothing has an inherent history. So when an emanation appears, it appears with a history. Just an appearance. So we can have emanations in our life that seem like they have this robust history to them, but it's just appearance. Something more than appearance.

And so when we start to look for these emanations, they appear everywhere. Like, I don't know, for me, I was here on Friday, preparing for a craving course on Saturday, and as I was preparing quite earnestly, at 10 a.m. a gentleman appeared outside our window, screaming and dancing. And he was drinking a red liquid from a water bottle, and wiggling his body, but incredibly intoxicated for 10 a.m. Right? Just kind of by himself. He just appeared out our window, screaming and dancing. To no one in particular, just doing his thing.

And when I got close to the window, I was trying to watch him and think about him. And then as he did that, he just threw down the water bottle and then walked away. He threw it in our garden outside and walked away.

But it was like a little teaching for me. Okay, this is what the craving mind looks like. There's this beautiful person with so much potential. And they're showing me what happens to you. In his mind, he probably is having a great time. But it's really dangerous, what's going on.

And then last night, I was thinking about this actually again, sitting at some random falafel restaurant or whatever, and he walked by again. Just another side of Brooklyn, like all the way into the depths of Park Slope. And he just was cruising on by.

And so for me, I just was thinking, okay, this is like, for me, it's functioning like an appearance, like an emanation for me. I'm not going to ask him. I kind of actually wanted, at that point when he had reappeared, I thought, okay, I want to talk to you. But then I just thought, I'm just going to have a view. That he's appearing to help me. To see, hey, Kyle, this could have been your life. If you didn't change your mind, this could have been you. Or, this is what the craving mind does to us. Or whatever, who knows what, whatever the teaching is for us.

So the point is, we should see them. We should be suspicious of their appearances in our life. They could be emanations helping us.

Okay. That's that. Thanks, everyone. Let's have some time for discussion now. Okay, I'll match people. Very nice. Let's do Ryan and Neal. And then Fran and Byron. And Alexis and Jose.
